boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Ezra Church record (July 28, 1864) in Atlanta Campaign [May-September 1864]. The cavalry expeditions of McCook and Stoneman begun on July 27 are context. The live NPS page labels the campaign "Morgan's Raid Into Kentucky" and dates it May-September 1864; neither field replaces the frozen campaign or battle interval. Campaign-wide totals are context and are not assigned to this record. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force fields name the Army of the Tennessee against two corps of the Army of Tennessee without counts; the live field reads zero. Cox says Lee's corps attacked, supported by Loring's and Walthall's divisions of Stewart's corps, and that Howard massed his artillery on the flank. Logan says prisoners reported the assault made by Hardee's and Lee's corps entire (his July 29 report says Hardee's and Lee's corps), that the enemy exceeded him in numbers, that he received about 1,000 men from Blair and Dodge, and that the enemy used one battery and he none.
claims.rationale: Conflicting identifications of the attacking corps and of the artillery used; no count of troops engaged is inspected and none is adopted. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: Logan says his line held the crest of a continuous ridge with a good field of fire. His July 29 report says the lines were protected only by hastily thrown logs and rails, while his campaign report says the troops had not had a moment to build even the rudest defences. Cox says Logan's men had made some cover, that the ground was high with a partly open slope, and that the Fifteenth Corps line bent back at nearly a right angle.
claims.rationale: Ground described by interested accounts, with an intra-source difference over cover; no map verification. The position was taken during the march and is not tagged inherited.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 3,562 (US 562; CS 3,000); the live field reads 5342 (US 700; CS 4642). Logan's July 29 and campaign reports both give his corps' loss as 50 killed, 439 wounded and 73 missing, aggregate 562; the first says 565 Confederates buried and about 200 unburied, the second over 600 buried; both judge the enemy loss at not less than 6,000 or 7,000. Cox says Howard reported under six hundred lost, fewer than the almost seven hundred Confederate dead buried by Logan, and that Howard estimated the enemy loss at five thousand.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The frozen US 562 equals Logan's Fifteenth Corps aggregate, which does not cover the reinforcing regiments of the other corps; whether the frozen figure derives from it is not established. The Confederate figures are estimates.

open_questions: Howard's army report, Blair's and Dodge's reports, S. D. Lee's report (opening read only), Stewart's report, Brown's and the Alabama regiments' reports and the compiled returns remain deferred. Hood's army report, a family for GA016-GA017, also covers July 28 but is not used as a family here under the three-family ceiling.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Cox's Atlanta (Scribner, 1882) is a second: a retrospective Union history by the Twenty-third Corps division commander, drawing on official reports and memoirs, so it is not independent of them. Logan's Fifteenth Corps reports, printed in Volume XXXVIII Part 3, are a third family (interested Union accounts). Official Records Series I Volume XXXVIII is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting. Campaign-wide strength and loss totals are context, not assigned to one record.
